title: Geometric Series for Matrices and Operators

problemStatement.formal: For T in a complete normed ring with ‖T‖ < 1: ∑' n, T^n = Ring.inverse (1-T)
problemStatement.plain: The Neumann series ∑ T^n converges to (1-T)⁻¹ for elements T with ‖T‖ < 1 in any complete normed ring.
whyMatters: Generalizes scalar geometric series to matrices and operators
Foundation of perturbation theory in functional analysis
Enables iterative methods in numerical linear algebra

proven: Perturbation of identity: ‖1-A‖ < 1 implies A invertible
knownResults.goal: Complete Neumann series formalization with gallery integration

insights: Units.oneSub constructs the inverse as ∑ T^n definitionally - use simp [Units.oneSub] to unfold
hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one requires NormedDivisionRing, but summable_geometric_of_norm_lt_one works for NormedRing
norm_pow_le requires NormOneClass (for n=0 term ‖1‖=1), norm_pow_le' works without it but needs n>0
In non-commutative rings: linear_combination requires CommSemiring, use abel for additive group manipulations instead
∑ k in range n syntax deprecated - use ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n
Ring.mul_inverse_cancel and Ring.inverse_mul_cancel provide left/right inverse identities for IsUnit elements

approaches.name: Units.oneSub + Ring.inverse bridge
approaches.description: Used Mathlib's Units.oneSub to construct the unit (1-T), then bridged to Ring.inverse via Ring.inverse_unit. Commutativity proved via left/right inverse identities and abel.
